design: IdentityRegistry(records=()) seeds records at construction, before the registry is shared, through the same immutable store as before (IdentityConflictError on a different record under a known identity, identical duplicates idempotent). identify_or_abstain builds its registry by seeding.

IdentityRegistry.register(record): under the registry lock, a record whose canonical_id is already known goes first to the unchanged immutability check (IdentityConflictError or no-op replay); otherwise, if its attributes carry any reserved Q1 key (principal_kind, status, roles: RESERVED_PRINCIPAL_ATTRIBUTES) it is refused with IdentityRegistrationDenied (OCORError, PermissionError; reason_code IDENTITY_PRIVILEGED_RECORD_REQUIRES_PROVISIONING) and nothing is stored or bound. Records without Q1 keys are admitted exactly as before.

IdentityProvisioningBoundary (WIP 6f98a15, unchanged checks) writes through IdentityRegistry._admit_provisioned, the reserved write path, under the registry lock after re-checking writer and identifiers; no public method admits a Q1 record after construction (public surface: register, get, add_alias, candidates, resolve, all_records).

Consumer test modules 0043, 0044, 0058, REM-0024, REM-0027, REM-0028: the post-construction registry.register loops become constructor seeding of the same IdentityRecord expressions; REM-0028 test bodies that added a record after directory() now seed IdentityRegistry with directory(...).all_records() plus that record; no other change (exact AST guard reports/tests/test_rem0031_consumer_registry_scope.py).

The reason code is defined in c2_identity.py, like the PROVISIONING_* codes of the boundary and the BREAK_GLASS_* codes of REM-0024: no sealed reason-code register, contract, schema or normative artefact is modified (PO point 3 condition not triggered); ocor_runtime/errors.py is unchanged.

findings_scope.REM-0024-IDENTITY-REGISTRY-WRITER-AUTHOR: the first writer of a new identity with privileged Q1 attributes is no longer accepted: register() refuses it, the boundary is the only runtime writer and authenticates/authorises it on real Keycloak/OPA.
findings_scope.REM-0031-REGISTRY-CONSUMER-SCOPE (2026-1: points 1-8 implemented within the closed scope; no consumer site outside the six modules needed a change (full suite 0 failures).

inputs_tree_definition: git rev-parse <commit>:inputs (tree della directory inputs/ immutabile)
normative_interpretations: 'Chiavi riservate Q1' is read as the exact attribute names principal_kind, status and roles (the identifiers read by c6/safety.py and c6/human_gate.py); presence of the key, with any value including empty or null, makes a new record privileged. Case-variant names are not reserved because no consumer reads them (tested as admitted).

An identical replay of an existing (seeded) Q1 record through register() is a no-op returning the stored record: it is the unchanged immutability check that the PO keeps first, and it adds nothing to the registry (tested).

The reserved write path _admit_provisioned is a private method used only by IdentityProvisioningBoundary; Python does not enforce privacy, so the guarantee is an API-surface guarantee (tested: no public method), not an in-process isolation boundary against code that already runs in the process.

requirement_results.command: a new record carrying any reserved Q1 key (principal_kind, status or roles, alone or together, any value) is refused by register() with IDENTITY_PRIVILEGED_RECORD_REQUIRES_PROVISIONING, registry unchanged (no record, no alias bound); the hostile first writer can no longer self-assign an approver role nor reach a real HumanGateCoordinator quorum (QUORUM_NOT_MET) (RED at 8dc56bd: DID NOT RAISE)

the immutability check stays first: a different record under a known identity (seeded Q1 or plain) still raises IdentityConflictError, an identical replay is a no-op; new records without Q1 keys (including case-different or similar non-reserved keys) are admitted unchanged

Q1 records enter only as constructor seeding (immutability preserved, identify_or_abstain via seeding) or through IdentityProvisioningBoundary; the public IdentityRegistry surface is exactly register/get/add_alias/candidates/resolve/all_records and none admits a Q1 record after construction
a writer authenticated by real Keycloak and authorised by real OPA with a signed bundle over SPIFFE mTLS creates a new Q1 record; receipt bound to writer, decision, bundle digest and correlation

hostile first writer (authenticated, not an authority) denied by the real policy; unauthenticated writer denied by real Keycloak; self-attribution denied by the boundary and independently by the real signed policy; invalid requests denied; registry unchanged in every case

writers registered as requester or approver (also by alias) denied; promotion, identical replay and bound alias updates denied; checks precede policy consultation and are repeated under the registry lock against concurrent admissions

real OPA or Keycloak paused, bundle absent or pinned to another digest, unreachable endpoint: PROVISIONING_AUTHORITY_UNAVAILABLE with cause, registry unchanged, recovery after unpause; every non-PERMIT effect and drifted decision is a denial

the signed, self-contained provisioning rule set rejects unsafe authority identifiers and every clause (action, namespace, self resource, authority set, effective principal, actor chain, delegation, capability) is evaluated on the real OPA

the six authorized consumer modules pass on the real stack after the seeding-only adaptation (label regression), and the exact AST guard proves the diff is limited to registry writes and construction (label guard)

residual_risks: In-process proof only: the registry and the boundary are in-memory; a caller with in-process access can still call private methods. This is not runtime conformance (PO point 8).

add_alias(canonical_id, alias) still binds new aliases to an existing record (unchanged behaviour, outside the closed scope); it creates no record and no Q1 attributes, and the resolver abstains on ambiguity.
Records without Q1 keys remain writable by any caller of register(); they carry no principal authority under the Q1 convention.
The provisioning authority list of the signed rule set is a composition parameter; its governance (who may be an authority) is outside this remediation.
